questions.stem: Calculate C(6, 3) and show that it matches the given value.
questions.explanation: This question tests the understanding of combinations and their calculation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to divide by only one factor of 3 instead of both 3 and 2.

questions.stem: Prove that C(5, 2) = C(5, 3). Show your work.
questions.explanation: This question tests the understanding of the identity C(n, r) = C( n, n-r).
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to assume that since the values are different when calculated directly, they are not equal according to the identity.

questions.stem: Calculate C(8, 4) + C(8, 5). Show your work and simplify if possible.
questions.explanation: This question tests the understanding of combinations and their calculation, along with the identity C( n, r) = C( n, n-r).
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to add the values without considering that C(8, 5) is equal to C(8, 3), which simplifies the problem.

questions.stem: Prove that C(n, r) = C(n-1, r-1) + C(n-1, r). Show your work.
questions.explanation: This question tests the understanding of a different identity related to combinations.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to assume that the two expressions are not equivalent without expanding and simplifying them.
